idea: When to replace old plumbing pipes
title: Galvanized Steel Pipes: Internal Corrosion Limits Flow
description: Galvanized steel pipes installed decades ago often fail from the inside out. Over time, reacting minerals and oxygen create internal rust buildup known as tuberculation. This corrosion layer thickens, severely restricting internal pipe diameter and reducing water pressure long before a visible leak occurs on the exterior. Furthermore, flaking rust causes discolored water at fixture outlets. If your property still relies on aging galvanized supply lines and experiences chronic pressure drop, inspect exposed pipe ends or cut sections. Replacing corroded galvanized sections with modern code-compliant materials restores volume and protects water quality.
image_prompt: A vertical 9:16 high-detail macro photograph showing a close-up cross-section cut of an old 3/4-inch galvanized steel water pipe held in a vise inside a realistic workshop setting. The cross-section clearly reveals heavy internal tuberculation and rust build-up inside the pipe bore, leaving only a tiny central opening for water flow, while the outer galvanized zinc shell remains largely intact. Clean neutral lighting, shallow depth of field, focused sharply on the inner corroded pipe profile. Clear visual negative space provided at the top third and bottom third for technical text overlays. Photorealistic texture, physically accurate metal wall thickness, no text, no logos, no watermarks, no artificial visual clutter.
visual_story: The viewer immediately notices the stark contrast between the intact exterior metal of the galvanized pipe and its severely choked interior bore. This visual demonstrates how internal tuberculation restricts water volume without obvious outer warning signs, teaching the viewer why pipe age and water performance matter more than exterior pipe appearance.

on_image_text.explanation: Galvanized steel corrodes from the inside out, choking water volume over time.
on_image_text.takeaway: Test pressure and inspect inner pipe walls, not just the exterior shell.
